note.explanation: Speed tells how much distance is covered per unit time. Velocity also tells the direction of motion, so it depends on displacement rather than distance. For example, a car moving north at 70 km h⁻¹ has speed 70 km h⁻¹ and velocity 70 km h⁻¹ north.
note.simple: Speed tells how fast something moves. Velocity tells how fast it moves and in which direction.
note.checkQuestion: What extra information does velocity give that speed does not?
note.title: Speed and Velocity
steps: For average speed, divide total distance by total time.
For average velocity, divide displacement by time.

note.answer: Average speed is total distance divided by total time. Average velocity is displacement divided by time and has a direction.

written.text: EXAMPLE 2.3: An eagle dives to the ground along a 300 m path with an average speed of 60 m s⁻¹. How long does it take to cover this distance?

rubric.how: Write v_av = 60 m s⁻¹.

written.text: Q2.7. A body is moving with uniform speed. Will its velocity be uniform? Give reason.
written.finalAnswer: Not necessarily; its direction may change, so its velocity may change.

rubric.why: Uniform speed alone does not establish uniform velocity.

rubric.why: Velocity depends on direction as well as speed.

written.text: Q2.3. For a complete trip, average velocity was calculated. Its value came out to be positive. Is it possible that its instantaneous velocity at any time during the trip had the negative value? Give justification of your answer.
written.finalAnswer: Yes. The body may move in the negative direction during part of the trip while its total displacement, and hence its average velocity, is positive.

rubric.why: The question asks whether this situation is possible.
rubric.how: Answer yes.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the velocity that may be negative.
rubric.how: State that instantaneous velocity may be negative during part of the trip.

rubric.why: Average velocity depends on the net displacement for the complete trip.
rubric.description: Relate average velocity to total displacement.
rubric.how: Explain that total displacement can remain positive.

rubric.why: The justification must connect the net displacement to the stated positive average velocity.
rubric.how: State that positive total displacement over the trip gives positive average velocity.

modelAnswer: The body may move in the negative direction during part of the trip, so its instantaneous velocity may be negative.
If its total displacement for the complete trip is positive, its average velocity will still be positive.

written.text: Q2.2 (b). Differentiate between speed and velocity.
written.finalAnswer: Speed is a scalar quantity: it is distance covered per unit time. Velocity is a vector quantity: it is displacement per unit time and has the direction of displacement.

rubric.why: The scalar or vector nature is a key difference.
rubric.how: Identify speed as a scalar quantity.

rubric.why: Speed is defined using distance and time.
rubric.how: State that speed is distance covered per unit time.

rubric.why: Velocity has direction and is a vector quantity.
rubric.how: Identify velocity as a vector quantity.

rubric.why: Velocity is based on displacement and includes direction.

rubric.how: State that velocity is displacement per unit time and has direction.

modelAnswer: Speed is a scalar quantity; it has magnitude but no direction.
Velocity is a vector quantity; it has both magnitude and direction.
Average velocity = displacement/time, and its direction is the direction of displacement.

written.text: Q2.8. A car travels 10 km with an average velocity of 20 m s⁻¹. Then it travels in the same direction through a diversion at an average velocity of 4 m s⁻¹ for the next 0.8 km. Determine the average velocity of the car for the total journey.

rubric.why: The first distance must be expressed consistently with the speed units.
rubric.how: Use 10 km = 10000 m.

rubric.why: The first time is found from distance divided by velocity.
rubric.how: Calculate 10000/20 = 500 s.

rubric.why: The second distance and velocity give the second travel time.
rubric.how: Calculate 800/4 = 200 s.

rubric.why: Average velocity uses the total displacement and total time.
rubric.description: Set up the total average velocity.
rubric.how: Add the distances and times, then divide total displacement by total time.

rubric.why: The final answer must be correctly evaluated and include a unit.
rubric.how: State 15.4 m s⁻¹.

examTips: Short questions may ask you to define speed, average speed, instantaneous speed, velocity, or uniform velocity. Write the definition clearly and include the correct quantity: distance for speed, displacement for velocity.
For a numerical question, write the known values, choose the equation, substitute with units, and state the final answer with its unit.
In a speed-and-velocity comparison, earn marks by stating that speed is scalar and velocity is vector, then explaining distance versus displacement and the role of direction.
For motion on a curved path, remember that velocity changes if direction changes, even when speed stays constant.

explain.title: Speed
explain.body: We are often interested to know how fast a body is moving. For this purpose, we have to find the distance covered in unit time which is known as speed. If a body covers a distance S in time t, its speed v will be written as: Speed = Distance/Time  v = S/t or S = vt. The speed is a scalar quantity.

explain.title: Average and instantaneous speed
explain.body: The speed of a vehicle that is shown by its speedometer at any instant is called instantaneous speed. Practically we make use of the average speed. It is defined as: Average speed = (Total distance covered)/(Total time taken) or v_av = S/t

explain.title: Velocity
explain.body: The net displacement of a body in unit time is called velocity. Average velocity = Displacement/Time or vector v_av = vector d/t. Velocity is a vector quantity. The direction of velocity vector v is the same as that of displacement vector d.

explain.title: Uniform and non-uniform velocity
explain.body: The velocity is said to be uniform if the speed and direction of a moving body does not change. If the speed or direction or both of them change, it is known as variable velocity or non-uniform velocity.

mistakes: Using distance instead of displacement when finding average velocity.
Forgetting that velocity includes direction, while speed does not.
Assuming that constant speed always means constant velocity; direction may still change.
Reversing the speed formula when finding time; use t = S/v.
Leaving out units from numerical answers.
